milestones.title: P0 — Laravel AI SDK Alignment & Runtime Boundary
milestones.description: Make Laravel AI SDK the package runtime substrate while preserving package-owned contracts, fluent APIs, and governance boundaries.

milestones.title: P1 — Core Workflow Infrastructure
milestones.description: Establish workflow composition, provider policy, queueing, and installation/publishing on top of the SDK-backed runtime boundary.

milestones.title: P2 — Conversation Memory & State
milestones.description: Provide package-owned conversation persistence, retention, and summarization with SDK context bridge compatibility.

milestones.title: P3 — Prompt & Tool Governance
milestones.description: Keep prompt and tool governance package-owned while executing through the SDK runtime.

milestones.title: P4 — Resilience & Orchestration Enhancements
milestones.description: Add retries, budgets, circuit breaking, lifecycle events, and failover telemetry around SDK-backed execution.

milestones.title: P5 — Vector & Retrieval
milestones.description: Expose a package-owned vector port with at least one implementation and a documented SDK-backed adapter strategy.

milestones.title: P6 — Compliance & Security Layer
milestones.description: Add encryption, redaction, retention, and secure defaults around package persistence and SDK-backed workflows.

milestones.title: P7 — Testing Harness & Observability
milestones.description: Provide package fakes, assertions, and optional observability extensions while keeping telemetry redacted and deterministic.

milestones.title: P8 — Context-Aware Scaffolding
milestones.description: Provide safe scaffolding commands that understand package conventions and Laravel AI SDK alignment assumptions.

milestones.title: P9 — Documentation & Patterns
milestones.description: Keep docs, examples, and architecture guidance aligned with the SDK-backed package design.

milestones.title: P10 — Multi-Agent Orchestration & Flagship Blueprints
milestones.description: Introduce package-owned multi-agent orchestration, governed delegation and handoff, provider-profile routing, and flagship blueprints built on top of the SDK-backed workflow substrate.

issues.title: P0-I1 Add laravel/ai as an explicit dependency + install/config wiring
issues.milestone: P0 — Laravel AI SDK Alignment & Runtime Boundary
issues.summary:
Add `laravel/ai` as an explicit Composer dependency and align package installation, service provider wiring, and configuration expectations so Laravel AI SDK becomes the package’s declared runtime substrate.

This issue does not expose Laravel AI SDK directly to package consumers. It establishes the dependency and installation assumptions required for the package to truthfully be described as built on Laravel AI SDK while keeping package-owned contracts intact.
issues.rationale:
The governing project documents already position the package as built on Laravel AI SDK, but the current implementation plan does not yet make that relationship operational. This creates architectural drift between stated intent and actual code structure.

Making Laravel AI SDK an explicit dependency is the first step in resolving that drift and enables later runtime bridge work to proceed on a stable foundation.

Ensure package boot/config flow remains compatible with Laravel AI SDK
Preserve package-owned public contracts and boundaries
acceptance_criteria: `composer.json` declares `laravel/ai` as a runtime dependency.
Install docs explicitly state that Laravel AI SDK is required and explain how it fits into the package architecture.
Package boot remains deterministic and fail-fast with config validation.
No SDK types are introduced into `src/Contracts/**` or README-documented public APIs.
Existing tests remain green after the dependency is introduced.
tests: Unit: N/A unless helper classes are introduced
Integration: container/service provider binding sanity; install/publish/config validation behavior
Contract: architecture/static checks proving no SDK type leakage into public contracts
Determinism controls: no network calls; no real provider execution
risks: Risk of accidentally leaking SDK types into package contracts
Risk of introducing hidden install complexity
Risk of diverging README/install docs from actual package boot behavior
docs: Update README install section
Update architecture docs to state Laravel AI SDK is the runtime substrate
Add migration note if the package is no longer intended to operate standalone

issues.title: P0-I2 Define package-owned runtime contracts + internal SDK runtime bridge
issues.milestone: P0 — Laravel AI SDK Alignment & Runtime Boundary
issues.summary:
Introduce a package-owned runtime seam for AI execution and implement the first internal Laravel AI SDK-backed runtime bridge behind that seam.

The package must not use SDK classes directly throughout its modules. Instead, prompts, tools, memory, pipelines, and blueprints should target package-owned contracts while actual execution is delegated to Laravel AI SDK internally.
issues.rationale:
The package must be built on Laravel AI SDK without leaking vendor SDK types into public contracts. The only sustainable way to satisfy both constraints is to centralize SDK interaction behind an internal bridge layer.

Without this seam, the project will either drift toward a standalone runtime or begin leaking SDK types through module boundaries.
scope: Define a package-owned runtime execution contract
Implement the first internal SDK-backed runtime class
Centralize direct SDK usage in one module
Introduce typed exceptions for runtime execution failures
out_of_scope: Full prompt, tool, memory, and vector mapping
acceptance_criteria: A package-owned runtime contract exists for AI execution.
Runtime request/result DTOs are package-owned and do not contain SDK types.
A Laravel AI SDK-backed runtime implementation exists behind the package-owned contract.
SDK-specific code is isolated to the runtime bridge module.
Runtime failures are wrapped in typed package exceptions with previous exceptions preserved.
No direct SDK dependency is added to package public contracts or DTOs.
tests: Unit: DTO validation and exception-wrapping behavior
Integration: container resolution for runtime bridge; delegation from package runtime contract to SDK-backed implementation
Contract: static/architecture checks for no vendor-type leakage
Determinism controls: use fakes/stubs, not real model calls
risks: Risk of creating too-thin an abstraction that adds little value
Risk of over-generalizing the runtime seam too early
Risk of SDK type leakage through exceptions, results, or helper utilities
docs: Update architecture docs with the runtime bridge layer
Document package-owned runtime contracts and their purpose

issues.title: P0-I4 Prompt repository → SDK instruction/message mapper

Map package-owned prompt repository output into Laravel AI SDK-compatible runtime inputs while preserving package-owned prompt abstractions.

The package should continue to own prompt templates, variables, and prompt selection/versioning. The SDK runtime should consume the rendered outcome via an internal mapper rather than by replacing the package prompt system.
issues.rationale: Prompt ownership is one of the package’s core differentiators. The package must keep prompt governance and template rendering package-owned, even though execution is handled by Laravel AI SDK.
